items.q: Which integral membrane transporter actively maintains phospholipid asymmetry by using ATP hydrolysis to translocate phosphatidylserine from the outer leaflet to the inner cytosolic leaflet?
items.exp: Flippases are P-type ATPases that specifically pump aminophospholipids (phosphatidylserine and phosphatidylethanolamine) inward from outer to inner leaflet against a concentration gradient.
r: Correct. P-type flippases pump phosphatidylserine inward from the outer leaflet.
Incorrect. Floppases pump lipids outward from inner to outer leaflet.
Incorrect. Scramblases randomly collapse asymmetry bidirectionally without ATP.
Incorrect. Anion channels transport ions, not lipids.

items.q: Lipid rafts are specialized, detergent-resistant membrane microdomains. Which two lipids are characteristically enriched within these rafts to maintain a liquid-ordered phase?
items.exp: Lipid rafts are tightly packed liquid-ordered domains enriched in cholesterol and saturated sphingolipids (such as sphingomyelin and glycosphingolipids), which organize transmembrane signaling complexes.
r: Correct. Cholesterol and sphingomyelin are the hallmark constituents of lipid rafts.
Incorrect. Cardiolipin is in mitochondria.
Incorrect. Triacylglycerols are stored in fat droplets, not plasma membranes.
Incorrect. Polyunsaturated lipids promote liquid-disordered bulk fluid phases.

items.q: The cardiac glycoside digoxin increases myocardial contractility by reversibly inhibiting the sodium-potassium ATPase. What immediate intracellular ion alteration drives this inotropic effect?
o: Elevated intracellular Na+ decreases NCX activity, raising intracellular Ca2+
Direct activation of sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release channels
Blockade of L-type voltage-gated calcium channels
Depletion of intracellular potassium activates troponin C
items.exp: Inhibiting Na+/K+-ATPase increases intracellular Na+, which reduces the trans-sarcolemmal Na+ gradient driving the 3Na+/1Ca2+ exchanger (NCX), resulting in secondary Ca2+ accumulation and enhanced cardiac contractility.
r: Correct. Elevated intracellular Na+ inhibits NCX calcium export, elevating intracellular Ca2+.
Incorrect. Digoxin does not bind ryanodine channels directly.
Incorrect. It does not block L-type calcium channels.
Incorrect. Intracellular K+ drops, but Ca2+ accumulation drives inotropy.
items.kp: Digoxin inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase pump, increasing intracellular Na+ and secondarily decreasing NCX Ca2+ export, boosting sarcoplasmic Ca2+ stores and contractility.

items.q: What is the most common pathogenic mutation in the CFTR gene responsible for cystic fibrosis, and what class of processing defect does it cause?
o: F508del (deletion of phenylalanine at position 508), causing Class II protein misfolding and ERAD degradation
G542X nonsense mutation, causing Class I absent protein synthesis
G551D missense mutation, causing Class III defective channel gating
R117H missense mutation, causing Class IV reduced channel conductance
items.exp: F508del is present in ~70% of CF alleles. The three-base-pair deletion of phenylalanine-508 prevents proper CFTR protein folding in the ER, routing it to ERAD proteasomal degradation so zero channel reaches the apical membrane.
r: Correct. F508del causes misfolding and premature ERAD proteasomal destruction (Class II).
Incorrect. G542X is a Class I stop codon mutation.
Incorrect. G551D is a Class III gating mutation treated with ivacaftor.
Incorrect. R117H is a Class IV conductance defect.
items.kp: CFTR F508del is a Class II mutation: the misfolded channel is caught by ER quality control and degraded by ERAD before reaching the cell surface.

items.q: Which glucose transporter isoform is insulin-responsive, undergoing translocation from intracellular vesicles to the plasma membrane in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue upon insulin signaling?
items.exp: GLUT4 is the insulin-sensitive glucose transporter expressed in striated muscle and adipose tissue. Insulin-stimulated Akt phosphorylation promotes exocytosis of GLUT4 storage vesicles to the cell surface.
r: Correct. GLUT4 translocates to plasma membranes in response to insulin and exercise.
Incorrect. GLUT1 is ubiquitous (RBCs, blood-brain barrier) and insulin-independent.
Incorrect. GLUT2 is bidirectional in liver and beta-cells, insulin-independent.
Incorrect. GLUT3 is in neurons with high glucose affinity.

items.q: Intestinal absorption of dietary glucose across the apical enterocyte membrane against its concentration gradient is mediated by which transporter and mechanism?
o: SGLT1 via secondary active sodium symport
items.exp: SGLT1 couples the downhill entry of two sodium ions (down an electrochemical gradient created by basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase) to the uphill import of one glucose or galactose molecule across the apical enterocyte membrane.
r: Correct. SGLT1 is a secondary active symporter using the sodium gradient.
Incorrect. GLUT2 is on the basolateral membrane for exit to blood via facilitated diffusion.
Incorrect. GLUT5 transports fructose, not glucose.
Incorrect. The Na+/K+-ATPase pump is basolateral.

items.q: Ivacaftor is a cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) potentiator. It is specifically indicated for which class of CFTR mutation?
o: Class III gating mutations (such as G551D) where channel reaches membrane but fails to open
Class I nonsense mutations with premature stop codons
Class II misfolding mutations with absent membrane expression
Class V promoter mutations with reduced transcript levels
items.exp: Ivacaftor is a channel potentiator that binds CFTR at the cell surface and increases channel open probability; it is highly effective for Class III gating defects like G551D.
r: Correct. Ivacaftor acts as a potentiator for gating mutations such as G551D.
Incorrect. Class I requires read-through agents.
Incorrect. Class II (F508del) requires correctors (lumacaftor, tezacaftor, elexacaftor) to reach membrane.
Incorrect. Class V requires splicing modulators.
items.kp: Ivacaftor is a CFTR potentiator that locks open the channel pore, clinically indicated for Class III gating mutations such as G551D.

items.q: Which ABC transporter family member functions as the multi-drug resistance protein 1 (MDR1 / P-glycoprotein), actively pumping lipophilic chemotherapy agents out of neoplastic cells?
items.exp: ABCB1 encodes P-glycoprotein (MDR1), an ATP-dependent efflux pump with broad substrate specificity that exports lipophilic xenobiotics and chemotherapy drugs (anthracyclines, vinca alkaloids), causing drug resistance.
r: Correct. ABCB1 encodes P-glycoprotein (MDR1).
Incorrect. ABCA1 exports cholesterol to ApoA-1 in Tangier disease.
Incorrect. ABCC2 (MRP2) exports conjugated bilirubin in Dubin-Johnson syndrome.
Incorrect. ABCG5/ABCG8 export plant sterols into bile.

Incorrect. ABCG8 exports sitosterol.
Incorrect. CFTR is an epithelial chloride channel.
